title: Reading supplier invoices into the accounts
summary: Turn thousands of messy supplier invoices a day into figures an accountant will sign.
context: Cubbon Traders buys from 4,000 suppliers, whose invoices arrive as PDFs, photos and spreadsheets. A vendor service reads them, with mixed accuracy. Accountants then match them to purchase orders before filing GST each month.
The numbers reported to management changed last quarter after a re-run, and no one could say why. The filing deadline is fixed, and a wrong tax credit can draw a notice.
must_handle: Each figure can be traced back to the file it came from.
A re-run with a better reader does not silently change a filed month.
A low-confidence invoice goes to a person, and the rest flow through.
The same invoice uploaded twice counts once.
The tax rules change, and past months must still reflect the rules of their time.
show_in_answer: The stages from an uploaded file to a reported figure.
The tables that hold invoices, their versions and their review state.
How a re-run works, and what it can and cannot change.
How a figure is traced back to its source.
